overview: Lebanon is a small country on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean, between Syria and Israel. Its capital and largest city is Beirut. Its coast was home to the ancient Phoenicians, who spread an early alphabet around the Mediterranean. Lebanon became independent from France in 1943. It has many religious communities, and political power is shared between them.

geography.text: Two mountain ranges run down Lebanon: the Mount Lebanon range near the coast and the Anti-Lebanon range along the border with Syria. Between them lies the fertile Beqaa Valley. The cedar tree, which grows in the mountains, appears on the national flag.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mediterranean on the coast, with snowy mountains in winter.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Migrating storks and eagles pass over in huge numbers.

history.text: Lebanon's coast was home to the Phoenician cities of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos, one of the oldest continuously inhabited towns in the world. After Ottoman rule and a French mandate, Lebanon became independent in 1943. A civil war from 1975 to 1990 devastated the country, and in 2020 a huge explosion in Beirut's port killed more than 200 people.

events.title: Phoenician cities
events.text: Tyre and Sidon become great trading cities.

events.title: French mandate
events.text: France takes control after the fall of the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Civil war
events.text: A civil war begins that lasts fifteen years.

events.title: Beirut explosion
events.text: A massive blast destroys much of Beirut's port.

government.text: Lebanon is a parliamentary republic in which power is shared among religious groups. By custom, the President is a Maronite Christian, the Prime Minister a Sunni Muslim and the Speaker of Parliament a Shia Muslim. Hezbollah, an armed group, has also been powerful. The country went without a President from 2022 until January 2025.

economy.text: Lebanon was once a banking and trading hub, but since 2019 it has suffered one of the worst economic crises in modern history, with its currency losing most of its value. The 2020 Beirut port explosion and conflict in 2024 added to the damage.

culture.text: Lebanon's culture mixes Arab, Mediterranean and French influences, and many people speak Arabic, French and English. Its food, from hummus to tabbouleh, is famous across the world. The cedar tree on its flag is an ancient symbol; cedars of Lebanon were used to build temples and ships.

items.title: Cedars of God
items.text: One of the last forests of the ancient cedars.

items.title: Baalbek
items.text: Roman temples with some of the largest stones ever used.

items.title: Byblos
items.text: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Mezze: hummus, tabbouleh, kibbeh and falafel.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Singers such as Fairuz and a long tradition of poetry and publishing.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Families gather for big Sunday lunches.

sport.text: Basketball is the most popular sport, and Lebanon has qualified for several Basketball World Cups. Football is also widely followed.

items.text: Lebanon played at the Basketball World Cup.

didYouKnow: Lebanon is one of the few places where you can ski in the morning and swim in the sea in the afternoon.
The word 'Bible' comes from Byblos, a Lebanese port that traded papyrus.
